subject: Integration follow-up: SDK auth, routing, and throttling plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@finovo.com>, Finovo Platform <infra@finovo.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: integration / quota & retry questions

Hi Lena / Finovo team,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking through your integration goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of needs we captured
- SDK + auth: you want a server-to-server service account flow (short-lived tokens), plus a fallback API key for dev environments.
- Routing: region-based affinity (US primary) and failover to secondary region; per-route quotas for embeddings vs generation.
- Structured output & tool calling: you plan to use our function-calling paths for enrichment calls and an embeddings-based reranker for search results.
- Quotas & throttling: expected steady traffic + periodic batch bursts; you need predictable behavior and clear guidance on 429s / retries / idempotency.

Action items we propose
1) You share a sample 24-hour traffic profile (QPS, burst patterns) — attached a CSV template.
2) We provide an integration checklist + SDK sample showing auth + request-id and idempotency usage.
3) Redwood to propose a per-route quota and fallback model mapping (cheaper reranker on burst).

Quick technical recommendations (first pass)
- Use short-lived OAuth service tokens for production; API keys for local/dev. Redwood SDK will handle token refresh transparently.
- Send a per-request tracing header: X-Request-Id (UUID v4). For operations that must not double-process (tool calls, payment-like ops) use X-Idempotency-Key.
- Retry guidance for 429s: exponential backoff with full jitter (base 200ms, max 8s) and honor Retry-After when present.
- For embeddings/reranker heavy routes, we recommend separate rate limits and an async batch path for bulk import jobs.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-integration-checklist.md, finovo-traffic-sample.csv

Next call: suggest a 30-minute technical deep dive next week (I’ll propose times).

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions (Redwood Inference)

Cc: Finovo Platform <infra@finovo.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: integration / quota & retry questions

Thanks Jordan — that matches our notes. A few details from our side to help you size recommendations: 

Traffic profile (high level)
- Steady state: ~20 requests/sec for search UX (each request triggers 1 embedding + 1 reranker call depending on query).
- Batch jobs: nightly indexing windows up to 120-150 req/sec for ~15 minutes (imports + recalc).
- Spike behavior: marketing events can double steady usage for short windows (~60–90s).

Functional constraints
- We will rely on function/tool calling for outbound enrichment (we require exactly-once effect for some enrichment ops).
- We prefer server-side short-lived tokens (OAuth). Can you confirm token TTLs and rotation approach?
- We need per-route quotas so that embeddings-heavy traffic cannot starve chat generation.

Questions
1) Does Redwood SDK provide a baked-in retry policy with idempotency integration? e.g., automatically attach idempotency keys for retries, dedupe on server?
2) For 429 responses, will you return Retry-After and suggest a recommended backoff window per-route?
3) For duplicate idempotency keys, what is server behavior (400/409/200)?

I attached a sample traffic CSV. We can also jump into a deep technical call — Tue/Wed next week works for me.

– Lena
Lena Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Finovo
lena.park@finovo.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap: integration / quota & retry questions (Finovo responses)

Folks — forwarding Finovo’s replies and traffic sample. Key asks: per-route quotas, clear Retry-After behavior, and server-side handling of idempotency keys for exactly-once enrichment calls.

My suggested internal plan:
- Marissa: put together a short SDK example (Node + Python) showing service-token flow, automatic X-Request-Id, and a sample retry wrapper that attaches X-Idempotency-Key for long-running tool calls. Include short notes on honoring Retry-After and backoff with jitter. Target: sample PR + snippet by EOD Monday.
- Karthik: recommend model-routing map (which model to route embeddings/reranker to under load), and an ops cost estimate for steady vs burst profiles from the CSV. Also look at dedicated pool / reserved capacity as an option for predictable bursts.
- Jordan: schedule a 30-min technical deep dive with Lena (I’ll propose times for Tue/Wed). Also confirm token TTLs and server-side idempotency semantics.

Notes on server behavior we should commit to:
- 429 responses will include Retry-After whenever applicable; SDK will use Retry-After as authoritative and fall back to exponential backoff with full jitter if header absent.
- For idempotent POSTs with X-Idempotency-Key, server will dedupe within a 24-hour window and return 409 on exact duplicates if the original request is still being processed; if original succeeded, return the original result (200). Confirm with platform team if any changes needed.

Marissa / Karthik — can you take the two items and loop back?

-Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@finovo.com>, Finovo Platform <infra@finovo.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Integration plan + SDK example for Finovo (auth, retries, request-id, quotas)

Hi Lena — thanks for the sample CSV. Attaching a short integration plan and a few artifacts to get you started. Attachments included: SOW-draft-v1.pdf, finovo-dataflow-diagram.png.

Highlights / implementation steps
1) Auth: we recommend OAuth service accounts with 15 minute access token TTL and automatic refresh via the Redwood SDK. For dev we support long-lived API keys with policy-scoped access.
2) Request tracing & idempotency
   - Per-request tracing header: X-Request-Id: <uuid4> (always set)
   - Idempotency for side-effecting ops: X-Idempotency-Key: <client-generated-uuid> (optional but required for exactly-once flows)
   - Server dedupe window: 24 hours. Duplicate within processing -> 409; duplicate after success -> 200 + original response payload.
3) Retry & 429 guidance
   - SDK default: exponential backoff with full jitter (base 200ms, cap 8s, 6 retries).
   - If server sets Retry-After: SDK uses that value before continuing backoff.
   - For bulk import endpoints, use the async bulk path which returns job ids and status polling to avoid front-door 429s.
4) Quotas & routing
   - We can do per-route quotas (embeddings, reranker, generation). We’ll propose an initial policy that reserves 60% of steady capacity for chat generation, 30% for embeddings during steady state, and 10% headroom. During batch windows the routing policy will route embedding calls to a lower-cost reranker model or queue them to the async import path.
5) Observability / tracing
   - We will provide per-request token-level cost and latency traces in the Console; include X-Request-Id to correlate.

Next steps & timeline
- Monday: we’ll post a short SDK snippet in the Drive folder.
- Tue/Wed: technical deep dive (Jordan will send invite).
- After deep dive: Redwood to send a formal routing/quota proposal and optional Dedicated pool pricing for index windows.

Attachments & links:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleLink
- SOW draft attached: SOW-draft-v1.pdf
- Dataflow diagram: finovo-dataflow-diagram.png

Example SDK usage (Node)
const reqId = uuidv4();
const idempotency = uuidv4();
await redwood.generate({
  model: 'redwood-gen-v1',
  prompt,
  headers: { 'X-Request-Id': reqId, 'X-Idempotency-Key': idempotency }
});

We’ll include a Python snippet in the Drive folder as well. If this looks good I’ll convert the SOW to a DocuSign-ready version and loop in Legal for a standard MSS+SLA.

Thanks —
